- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if price is falling sharply.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75% of recent high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for next 3 days.  
- If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 5 days, model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion bias: forecast = 0.8×previous + 0.2×true if true is lower.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts early in the cycle (first 5–7 days); reduce first 5 forecast points by 1–2% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.50” values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–7 days to compensate for low sentiment bias.
